question: In Python, a for loop can be used to iterate over the elements of a list.
A while loop in Python will execute its block of code only once regardless of the condition.
In a for loop, the loop variable automatically takes the value of each element in the iterable during each iteration.
The range(5) function in a for loop generates the sequence of numbers from 1 to 5 inclusive.
Nested loops allow you to iterate over multi-dimensional data structures by placing one loop inside another.
Using a break statement inside a loop will immediately terminate the loop regardless of the loop condition.
The continue statement in a loop skips the current iteration and exits the loop entirely.
In Python, a for loop can have an else clause that executes only if the loop completes without encountering a break statement.
An infinite loop occurs when the loop's terminating condition is never met, causing the loop to run indefinitely.
List comprehensions in Python are a form of loops that can include conditional statements to filter items, making them equivalent to nested loops in complexity.
